rules_evaluated.evidence: FIXED THIS SESSION. Before edit, L141 read `[checked:2026-07-30 result:OK due:2027-01-30]` on the Willison 'Designing agentic loops' URL — 2026-07-30 + 6 months = 2027-01-30 exactly, the literal 'checked+6mo' computation §11a bans by name ('Never checked+6mo... the arithmetic grants a three-weeks-from-stale source a fresh year'). A prior technical-judge instance (this same instance file, pre-overwrite) filed this as REVISE/blocking with matching reasoning; the file's Quality line records it as 'technical PASS (verify-refuted)', but no maintainer-block accept-note addresses the DUE-field computation specifically — the adjacent prose ('No compendium rule waives the clock here; this is a maintainer decision') covers only the §2 question of citing evidence past its freshness window (same shape as the Cherny precedent), not the §11a question of how `due` must be computed once that decision is made. Git blame (`git show a4920c15`) shows the checked+6mo value was introduced when a Claude-authored commit converted this citation from a delegated stamp (`due:none`, correct) into an owned one, with no due-date reasoning in the commit message — an authoring-time slip, not a considered exception. A same-day sibling case (commit 7fb973dd, `curriculum/lectures/test-and-learn.md`, Ronacher stamp) hit the identical defect and was fixed by recomputing due from the source's publication date; applied the identical fix here: due recomputed as publication (2025-09-30) + 6 months = 2026-03-30, `result:OK` left unchanged (matches the Ronacher precedent's fix shape exactly — recompute due, don't touch result). Re-read `curriculum/source-freshness-format.md` before fixing: 'Default = the source's publication date + 6 months... not checked + 6 months, which would hand a five-month-old post a fresh year every time someone re-opens it' — confirms the fix direction. Harm now closed: `source-freshness.sh` will read this stamp as overdue (due < today) rather than silently fresh until 2027, matching the honest state the maintainer's own adjacent prose already discloses.
